Are you passionate about developing and strengthening your database system skills, and like questioning the status quo for the benefit of Danske Bank and its customers?

Then join our team and become our new Platform Database Engineer

We are looking for a profile who will be part of a global team responsible for building, configuring, and maintaining Danske Bank’s mainframe database systems. Our primary design goals are service availability, efficiency, and resilience, underpinned by the architectural principle of cloned infrastructure, system configurations and applications. The position is in Denmark, Copenhagen central or Århus.

The role

• Perform database maintenance tasks, software upgrades coupled with administration and tuning to support our database environments and database tooling.

• Establish, maintain, and implement policies and procedures pertaining to database management, disaster recovery, security, maintenance, compliance, and utilization.

• Investigate new database functionality to explore and exploit new opportunities.

• Collect and analyze data to ensure optimal performance of the system.

• Be proactive in problem diagnostics and resolution and to challenge the existing where improvements could make sense.

• Encourage and ensure collaboration across teams and vendors to provide guidance and manage different tasks with a “can-do” attitude.

• Interact with vendors to troubleshoot and drive enhancements to product in our portfolio.

• Proactively help control risk and compliance and lead by example.

Do you have what it takes?

We need a new colleague, who takes ownership as an individual, but also one who teams up. You need to be curious about learning new technology, and we need a person who is not afraid of challenging status quo or taking personal initiative to help us drive superior solutions for the benefit of the Bank and its customers.

We would like to see the following core skills:

• Have some experience of installing, maintaining, and supporting database systems and related software products.

• Feel comfortable working with critical data on several platforms.

• Strong analytical mind and a determination to help drive/facilitate complex problems to resolution.

• Experience with design, configuration, and support of systems in an environment running mission critical 24*7*365 workload.

• Experience working with Public Cloud.

• Have an open mind and an inherent curiosity that can be a constant drive in your professional development.

Additional Preferred Skills

• Degree related to Computer Science or IT

• Equivalent education with required experience

What can we offer?

We are a leading technology team with a global international and modern scene. We have global colleagues and workdays can easily be a flexible mix of physical and virtual presence. We will offer you many opportunities to grow your career and develop your competencies. We have inspirational leaders, who will support you to succeed, and we offer you great flexibility and autonomy.

Interested?

Does this sound like you? Then we look forward to hearing from you. We screen the applications on an ongoing basis, and we encourage you to apply as soon as possible. For questions, please contact Jesper Hollitsch Poulsen on JHP@danskebank.dk.

Kassow Robots is a Danish company that develops and manufactures unique 7-axis collaborative robots for a wide range of industrial applications. Since 2022, we have been part of Bosch Rexroth, a leading global automation company within the Bosch Group.

Are you passionate about cutting-edge technology and hands-on problem solving? In our Assembly and Repair Department, you will take on an important role, working with colleagues to assemble, repair, and improve complete robot systems.

At our young technology company, you will join a diverse and dedicated team of passionate colleagues who make a real difference every day. You’ll experience a dynamic work environment where collaboration, innovation, and quality are at the heart of everything we do.

Your Primary Responsibilities

• Inspect, analyze, and troubleshoot robotic systems and equipment

• Read repair manuals and collaborate with engineers and other specialists

• Run tests, interpret results, and provide effective recommendations

• Write reports, safety regulations, and preventative maintenance plans

• Source and replace faulty parts and components

• Perform both mechanical and electrical assembly of robot systems

• Support manufacturing and development engineers in ongoing projects

• Handle service requests via our support system

• Stay up to date with advancements in the field and attend workshops as needed

What We’re Looking For

• Practical experience with installation, repair, and troubleshooting of complex systems, ideally including electronics and cabling

• Strong problem-solving skills and ability to learn quickly

• A quality-conscious, systematic, and hands-on approach to work

• Ability to manage multiple tasks simultaneously and thrive in a dynamic environment

• Excellent team player with strong communication skills

• A customer-oriented mindset with a focus on delivering reliable solutions

What We Offer

• Comprehensive training in our robot systems and installations

• A collaborative and innovative work environment in a growing tech company

• Opportunity to work with state-of-the-art robotics

• Personal and professional development through workshops and knowledge sharing

• A role where your contributions directly impact the company’s success

📍 Workplace: All work takes place at our company headquarters in Kastrup.

Shape the future of education technology

At IST, we're building the cloud platform that powers educational solutions used by more than five million users across Europe. Unlike most cloud teams, we run our own cloud — on our own hardware, in our own data center. That means the abstraction stops with us: when a node misbehaves, there's no support ticket to a hyperscaler.

There's a rack, and someone who knows it.

We're looking for a Cloud Engineer who finds that appealing rather than daunting.

About the role

As a Cloud Engineer, you'll help design, build and operate the IST Cloud Platform — from the automation and orchestration layers our developers build on, all the way down to the switches, servers and cabling that carry it. You'll do this together with our Cloud Engineering team, architects, developers and stakeholders, whether the work happens at a keyboard or in a rack.

In practice, around a quarter of your time will be spent physically on site in the data center. Not as a separate duty, but as a natural part of the work: expanding capacity for a new cluster the team has just automated, replacing a switch that's been throwing errors in your own monitoring, tracing a network issue that turns out to be a cable rather than a config. Owning the platform end to end is what makes this role different from a pure cloud position.

The role is based at our office in Roskilde, Denmark, with the primary data center within reach. Some travel is required, primarily to our office in Växjö, Sweden.

Key responsibilities

• Design, build and operate the IST Cloud Platform across the full stack — from physical hardware to the self-service tooling our developers use

• Automate VMs, containers, storage and networking using Ansible, Terraform, Puppet and PowerShell DSC

• Plan and carry out capacity expansions: from sizing and procurement to racking, cabling, provisioning and putting the capacity into production

• Diagnose and resolve issues wherever they originate — including replacing switches, disks and other failed components on site, and handling firmware, BIOS and driver lifecycle across the fleet

• Support reliable, scalable developer platforms, CI/CD pipelines, orchestration and self-service tools

• Manage databases, object storage and monitoring/logging stacks, with observability that spans both the platform and the hardware underneath it

• Contribute to access, identity and compliance work in line with ISO, PCI and internal policies, including physical access and site security

• Ensure robust backup and disaster recovery plans are in place, tested against real hardware failure scenarios

• Coordinate with hardware vendors and support partners (Dell, Cisco and similar) on spare parts, RMAs and escalations

Your profile

You have a bachelor's or master's degree in computer science, network engineering or a related field, or equivalent practical experience, along with solid experience in cloud engineering, infrastructure automation and DevOps practices.

Just as importantly, you're comfortable at both ends of the stack. You can discuss platform architecture with our developers in the morning and spend the afternoon in the rack with a screwdriver, and you see those as the same job rather than two different ones. Working in a data center environment — noisy, cold, occasionally at short notice — is something you take in stride.

We also look for:

• Hands-on experience with server, storage and network hardware — Cisco, Dell, KVM, VMware or similar

• Practical understanding of data center fundamentals: power, cooling, rack design, structured cabling

• Strong knowledge of security, compliance and governance in cloud environments

• Strategic thinking and the ability to translate business needs into technical solutions

• Excellent verbal and written communication skills in English

• A collaborative, decisive and pragmatic approach to problem-solving

• A valid driver's license and the ability to reach the data center when needed

What we offer

This is a full-time, permanent position. We apply an office-first policy, and given the hands-on nature of this role, regular physical presence at the office and in the datacenter is part of the job. Within that framework, there's room for flexibility on the days where your work doesn't require you on site.

You'll join an international and collaborative environment where you'll have real ownership, influence over strategic technology decisions, and the chance to help shape the future of learning.

Apply

Applications are reviewed continuously. For questions, contact Bengt Welin bengt.welin@ist.com or HR@ist.com. Please note that a background check is part of the recruitment process.

Welcome to apply!

jobs.occupation: Special Consultant for HealthTech Innovation and Venture Development – DTU Entrepreneurship
jobs.description:
DTU is strengthening its collaboration with Rigshospitalet in the Technical University Hospital (TUH). We aim to create a coherent innovation pathway from identification of unmet clinical needs through exploration, prototyping and validation to startup formation and commercialisation.

DTU Entrepreneurship is looking for an experienced Special Consultant to coordinate and further develop this HealthTech innovation pipeline.

You will work at the intersection of technology, healthcare, education, entrepreneurship and commercialisation. A central part of the role will be to connect existing DTU and hospital activities into a functioning pathway. We will ensure that promising HealthTech opportunities can progress between educational programmes, clinical environments, prototyping activities and venture development.

You will collaborate closely with DTU Entrepreneurship, TUH, Rigshospitalet, DTU Skylab and TUH Skylab, relevant DTU departments, clinicians, course responsibles, students and external ecosystem partners.

The job
You will coordinate DTU Entrepreneurship's contribution to the TUH HealthTech innovation initiative. Further contribute hands-on to the development and maturation of selected HealthTech opportunities.

Your primary tasks will include:

• Coordinating the HealthTech innovation initiative across DTU, hospitals and other key stakeholders.
• Developing and maintaining a HealthTech innovation pipeline from clinical need identification to venture creation.
• Supporting the identification and prioritisation of unmet clinical needs in collaboration with clinicians and other experts.
• Providing business development and commercialisation support to selected HealthTech projects, including market assessment, business models, partnerships and funding.
• Mentoring multidisciplinary student teams and potential founders through teaching, coaching and venture development activities.
• Engaging relevant external stakeholders and contributing to the continued development of DTU's HealthTech innovation ecosystem.
You will have a high degree of independence in planning and executing activities while working closely with the TUH leadership and key stakeholders.

We are looking for a senior profile with strong experience in HealthTech innovation, entrepreneurship and commercialisation.

We expect that you have:

• An MSc degree in engineering, technology or a related scientific discipline.
• Proven experience in developing and commercialising healthcare technologies from early-stage innovation to venture creation or market implementation.
• Experience working across the healthcare, university and startup ecosystems.
• Strong business development and commercialisation skills, including market assessment, business model development and stakeholder engagement.
• Experience leading complex projects involving multiple stakeholders.
• Excellent communication, collaboration and facilitation skills.
• Professional proficiency in Danish and English.
It will be an advantage if you have:

• Founder or senior leadership experience from a MedTech or life-science company.
• A PhD or additional education in business, innovation or entrepreneurship.
• Experience with fundraising, partnerships or innovation funding programmes.
What we offer in return
You will become part of DTU Entrepreneurship and work closely with colleagues across DTU and the Technical University Hospital collaboration.

The position offers an opportunity to play a central role in developing a new university-hospital HealthTech innovation pipeline. This means to work with projects spanning clinical unmet needs, engineering, entrepreneurship, prototyping and venture creation.

You will interact with a broad ecosystem of clinicians, researchers, students, entrepreneurs, industry representatives, investors and innovation organisations. You will contribute to establishing a capability intended to remain beyond the present project period.

The role combines strategic development with hands-on engagement in individual innovation and venture projects.

Salary and appointment terms 
The appointment will be based on the collective agreement with the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations (AC). You are employed as an Senior Officer or Senior Executive Officer. In addition, supplements can be negotiated in accordance with DTU’s salary structure for academic staff employed in technical-administrative positions at DTU (AC TAP): www.inside.dtu.dk/en/human-resources/during-employment/salary/salary-structures. 

The position is a fixed-term, part-time Special Consultant position until 31 December 2028. The expected employment is 29,6 hours per week. The starting date is 1 November 2026 or as soon as possible thereafter.

Because the activities vary over the project period, the position requires flexibility in the organisation of working time. There will be periods of increased activity around project milestones, educational activities, stakeholder engagement and international collaboration.

Application and contact
Please submit your online application no later than Tuesday, 27 October 2026. Open the “Apply now” link, fill out the form and attach your motivated application, CV and exam certificates. 

If you would like additional information about the position, please contact Professor Thomas Howard on thow@dtu.dk.

Applications received after the deadline will not be considered.

All interested candidates irrespective of age, gender, disability, race, religion or ethnic background are encouraged to apply. As DTU works with research in critical technology, which is subject to special rules for security and export control, open-source background checks may be conducted on qualified candidates for the position.

DTU Entrepreneurship is amongst the leading international entities in technology entrepreneurship and helps develop an entrepreneurial culture across DTU. As part of a dynamic and evolving ecosystem, we combine practice-oriented education and research in entrepreneurship with real start-up opportunities from all DTU departments. With rigorous research at its core, the Center builds the entrepreneurial capabilities of students, industry leaders, academics and policymakers to address unsolved problems, and together create new knowledge, methodologies and initiatives. We enable ethically minded entrepreneurs to build solutions that benefit people, society and the world. The Center experiments with new entrepreneurial methodologies and activities to push boundaries within research and education.

DTU – For the benefit of society since 1829
DTU is one of Europe's leading elite technical universities. Through research and education at an international top level, we create solutions to the major societal challenges of our time and help secure Europe's global leadership in sustainable technological development. Since Hans Christian Ørsted founded DTU almost 200 years ago, our mission has remained the same: We develop and create value through the natural and technical sciences for the benefit of society. DTU has 13,800 students, 1,600 PhD students, and 6,500 employees. We work in an international environment and have an inclusive, stimulating, and informal work culture. DTU has campuses in all parts of Denmark and in Greenland and collaborates with the best universities around the world.

jobs.occupation: PhD Scholarship in Machine Learning for Non-Stationary and Non-Static Nano-Tomography - DTU Compute
jobs.description:
Recent advances in machine learning and deep learning are opening new possibilities for computational imaging, including the reconstruction of complex 3D structures from experimental imaging data. In this fully funded PhD project at DTU Compute, you will develop novel learning-based methods for X-ray nano-tomography. As state-of-the-art synchrotron imaging systems push towards ever higher spatial resolution, even minute positioning errors, mechanical drift, and sample deformations become sources of image degradation. The central challenge is to reconstruct accurate 3D and 4D representations of samples while accounting for positional uncertainties during image acquisition and changes in sample shape over time.

The project will bring together neural representations, inverse problems, geometric modeling, and computational imaging to address fundamental challenges in nano-tomography. Rather than correcting acquisition errors and sample deformations as separate preprocessing steps, you will investigate how to model and estimate the sample structure, acquisition geometry, and deformation jointly from the measured data.

The position is based at DTU Compute and conducted in close collaboration with EPFL and the Paul Scherrer Institute (PSI) in Switzerland, one of the leading centers for synchrotron X-ray imaging. As a PhD student, you will work in an international research environment spanning DTU, EPFL, and PSI, combining expertise in both machine learning and computational imaging with access to experimental data and advanced imaging facilities. Research visits to Switzerland are planned as part of the project.

Responsibilities

• Develop novel machine learning and deep learning methods for X-ray nano-tomography, which jointly reconstruct sample structure, acquisition geometry, and deformation fields from inconsistent projection data.
• Investigate neural field representations for 3D and 4D imaging, including models that capture changes in sample geometry over time, and explore hybrid approaches combining learning-based methods with physical models of image formation and tomographic reconstruction.
• Validate and evaluate the developed methods using experimental nano-tomography data, initially focusing on integrated circuits.
• Collaborate with researchers at DTU, PSI, and EPFL, and participate in international research visits and scientific activities.
• Publish research results in leading journals and conferences in machine learning, computer vision, and computational imaging.
• Contribute to research-based teaching and supervision of MSc and BSc student projects.
• Participate in activities within the Center for Quantification of Imaging Data from MAX IV (QIM), including workshops, training courses, and interdisciplinary research collaborations.
Qualifications
You are curious and motivated by developing new machine learning methods to solve challenging problems in computational imaging. A strong background in machine learning and deep learning is particularly important. We welcome candidates from computer science, applied mathematics, physics, engineering, and related disciplines who are interested in combining modern learning methods with mathematical modeling and real-world experimental data. The candidate should be able to work independently, contribute effectively to an interdisciplinary research team, and communicate scientific ideas clearly in written and spoken English.

To succeed in this position, you are expected to have:

• A master's degree in computer science, applied mathematics, physics, engineering, or a related discipline.
• A strong background in machine learning and deep learning, including experience developing, implementing, or evaluating learning-based models.
• Experience with scientific programming, preferably in Python, and familiarity with relevant machine learning frameworks.
• A solid understanding of mathematical modeling, optimization, or numerical methods.
Experience in one or more of the following areas is an advantage:

• Neural representations, implicit neural fields, or other coordinate-based representations.
• Computer vision, 3D vision, geometric modeling, or structure-from-motion.
• Inverse problems, image reconstruction, or physics-informed machine learning.
• Image registration, motion estimation, or deformable modeling.
• Image processing, image analysis, or tomographic reconstruction.
• Knowledge of X-ray imaging and tomography is beneficial but not required. 
You must have a two-year master's degree (120 ECTS points) or a similar degree with an academic level equivalent to a two-year master's degree.

Approval and Enrolment 
The scholarship for the PhD degree is subject to academic approval, and the candidate will be enrolled in one of the general degree programmes at DTU. For information about our enrolment requirements and the general planning of the PhD study programme, please see DTU's rules for the PhD education. 

We offer
DTU is a leading technical university globally recognized for the excellence of its research, education, innovation and scientific advice. We offer a rewarding and challenging job in an international environment. We strive for academic excellence in an environment characterized by collegial respect and academic freedom tempered by responsibility.

At DTU Compute, we have a large focus on creating a good working environment. Our work with diversity and inclusion is an essential part of that. We believe that having a good working environment is a necessary foundation to provide excellent research, teaching, supervision and innovation.

At DTU Compute, we have about 140 PhD students. We offer several events and activities for all our PhD students such as annual PhD Bazaar, onboarding course where you will meet other PhD students, and you can join our PhD Club that organizes BBQs, board games events, lunches etc. 

Salary and appointment terms 
The appointment will be based on the collective agreement with the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations. Please see DTU’s salary structure for scientific staff: www.inside.dtu.dk/en/human-resources/during-employment/salary/salary-structures. 

The period of employment is 3 years. The starting date is 1 March 2027 (or according to mutual agreement). The position is a full-time position.

You can read more about career paths at DTU here.

Further information 
Further information may be obtained from Hans Martin Kjer, hmkj@dtu.dk. 

You can read more about DTU Compute at www.compute.dtu.dk.

If you are applying from abroad, you may find useful information on working in Denmark and at DTU at DTU – Moving to Denmark. Furthermore, you have the option of joining our monthly free seminar “PhD relocation to Denmark and startup “Zoom” seminar” for all questions regarding the practical matters of moving to Denmark and working as a PhD at DTU. 

Application procedure 
Your complete online application must be submitted no later than 16 November 2026 (23:59 Danish time). Applications must be submitted as one PDF file containing all materials to be given consideration. To apply, please open the link "Apply now", fill out the online application form, and attach all your materials in English in one PDF file. The file must include:

• A letter motivating the application (cover letter)
• Curriculum vitae 
• Grade transcripts and BSc/MSc diploma (in English) including official description of grading scale
You may apply prior to obtaining your master's degree but cannot begin before having received it.

Applications received after the deadline will not be considered.

All interested candidates irrespective of age, gender, disability, race, religion or ethnic background are encouraged to apply. As DTU works with research in critical technology, which is subject to special rules for security and export control, open-source background checks may be conducted on qualified candidates for the position.

DTU Compute
DTU Compute – Department of Applied Mathematics and Computer Science – is an internationally recognised academic environment with over 400 employees and 10 research sections. We broadly cover digital technologies within mathematics, data science, computer science, and computer engineering, including artificial intelligence (AI), machine learning, internet of things (IoT), chip design, cybersecurity, human-computer interaction, social networks, fairness, and data ethics. Our research is rooted in basic research and centres on mathematical models of the physical and virtual world, as a basis for the analysis, design, and implementation of complex systems. We focus on ensuring that our research results contribute to creating a better society by supporting areas such as health, green transition, energy supply, and life science. We collaborate with universities, public and private organisations, and companies in Denmark and abroad, and through DTU’s startup ecosystem, we encourage innovation and entrepreneurship. We have a strong ethical, human, and sustainable approach that ensures integrity in our work. Therefore, we strive for and take responsibility for driving the democratisation of digital technologies, so that everyone has the opportunity to actively participate in the development, and we ensure a continued open, democratic, and inclusive society for the benefit of all. At DTU Compute, we value diversity, inclusion, and a flexible work-life balance. Read more here: www.compute.dtu.dk.

DTU – For the benefit of society since 1829
DTU is one of Europe's leading elite technical universities. Through research and education at an international top level, we create solutions to the major societal challenges of our time and help secure Europe's global leadership in sustainable technological development. Since Hans Christian Ørsted founded DTU almost 200 years ago, our mission has remained the same: We develop and create value through the natural and technical sciences for the benefit of society. DTU has 13,800 students, 1,600 PhD students, and 6,500 employees. We work in an international environment and have an inclusive, stimulating, and informal work culture. DTU has campuses in all parts of Denmark and in Greenland and collaborates with the best universities around the world.

jobs.occupation: PhD Position in Entrepreneurship, AI, and Labor Market Disruption - DTU Entrepreneurship
jobs.description:
Are you interested in exploring the following questions? 

• How are artificial intelligence (AI) and automation reshaping individuals' transitions to entrepreneurship?
• How do individuals' skills, experience, and technological readiness influence the types of businesses they create and their subsequent performance?
• How do these patterns vary across countries and institutional contexts?
DTU Entrepreneurship invites applications for a three-year PhD scholarship as part of an international research project entitled The New Landscape of Necessity Entrepreneurship: Understanding Entrepreneurial Transitions in an Era of AI- and Automation-Driven Labor Market Disruption.

The project investigates how AI and automation reshape entrepreneurial transitions, with particular attention to individuals who start businesses following unemployment. The PhD candidate will join an international research team involving Associate Professor Argyro (Iro) Nikiforou at the Technical University of Denmark (DTU), Professor Marc Gruber at École Polytechnique Fédérale de Lausanne (EPFL), Switzerland, and Professor John C. Dencker at Northeastern University, USA. Funded by the Swiss National Science Foundation (SNSF), the project combines large-scale surveys, Danish administrative registry data, and qualitative interviews across Denmark, Switzerland, and Greece.

The position offers an opportunity to contribute to cutting-edge entrepreneurship research, work with rich international datasets, and collaborate with leading scholars in the field.

Responsibilities and qualifications
Your primary responsibility will be to conduct high-quality research within the international project, with opportunities to develop your own research questions within its overall scope.

Your tasks will include:

• Developing research questions and theoretical frameworks concerning entrepreneurship, human capital, AI, and labor market transitions.
• Applying quantitative and qualitative research methods to investigate entrepreneurial transitions and outcomes.
• Collecting, managing, and analyzing quantitative data, including large-scale surveys and Danish registry data.
• Contributing to the design and implementation of surveys and qualitative interviews in collaboration with international research partners.
• Preparing research papers for submission to leading international academic journals.
• Presenting research findings at international conferences and contributing to dissemination activities targeting policymakers and other stakeholders.
• Collaborating with researchers at DTU, EPFL, Northeastern University, and other project partners.
We are looking for a highly motivated candidate with a strong interest in entrepreneurship research and technological change.

We expect you to have:

• A Master’s degree.
• A strong interest in developing quantitative research and analytical skills.
• Excellent written and spoken English communication skills.
• The ability to work independently and collaboratively in an international research environment.
The following qualifications would be considered an advantage, but are not required:

• Experience working with large-scale datasets, registry data, or longitudinal data.
• Experience with statistical software such as Stata or R, and familiarity with econometric techniques, including regression analysis and panel data methods. 
• Experience with survey design, qualitative interviewing, or mixed-methods research.
You must have a two-year master's degree (120 ECTS points) or a similar degree with an academic level equivalent to a two-year master's degree.

Approval and Enrolment 
The scholarship for the PhD degree is subject to academic approval, and the candidate will be enrolled in one of the general degree programmes at DTU. For information about our enrolment requirements and the general planning of the PhD study programme, please see DTU's rules for the PhD education. 

Assessment
The assessment of applicants will be conducted by Associate Professor Argyro (Iro) Nikiforou, who will serve as the principal supervisor.

We offer
DTU is a leading technical university globally recognized for the excellence of its research, education, innovation and scientific advice. We offer a rewarding and challenging job in an international environment. We strive for academic excellence in an environment characterized by collegial respect and academic freedom tempered by responsibility.

Salary and appointment terms
The appointment will be based on the collective agreement with the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations. Please see DTU’s salary structure for scientific staff: www.inside.dtu.dk/en/human-resources/during-employment/salary/salary-structures. 

The period of employment is 3 years. The expected starting date is as soon as possible or as agreed with the successful candidate.

You can read more about career paths at DTU here.

Further information
Further information may be obtained from Associate Professor Argyro (Iro) Nikiforou, DTU Entrepreneurship, Technical University of Denmark, at argnik@dtu.dk.

You can read more about DTU Entrepreneurship at www.entrepreneurship.dtu.dk.

If you are applying from abroad, you may find useful information on working in Denmark and at DTU at DTU – Moving to Denmark. Furthermore, you have the option of joining our monthly free seminar “PhD relocation to Denmark and startup “Zoom” seminar” for all questions regarding the practical matters of moving to Denmark and working as a PhD at DTU. 

Application procedure 
Your complete online application must be submitted no later than 8 November 2026 (23:59 Danish time). Applications must be submitted as one PDF file containing all materials to be given consideration. To apply, please open the link "Apply now", fill out the online application form, and attach all your materials in English in one PDF file. The file must include:

• A letter motivating the application (cover letter)
• Curriculum vitae 
• Grade transcripts and BSc/MSc diploma (in English) including official description of grading scale
You may apply prior to obtaining your master's degree but cannot begin before having received it.

Applications received after the deadline will not be considered.

All interested candidates irrespective of age, gender, disability, race, religion or ethnic background are encouraged to apply. As DTU works with research in critical technology, which is subject to special rules for security and export control, open-source background checks may be conducted on qualified candidates for the position.

DTU Entrepreneurship is amongst the leading international entities in technology entrepreneurship and helps develop an entrepreneurial culture across DTU. As part of a dynamic and evolving ecosystem, we combine practice-oriented education and research in entrepreneurship with real start-up opportunities from all DTU departments. With rigorous research at its core, the Center builds the entrepreneurial capabilities of students, industry leaders, academics and policymakers to address unsolved problems, and together create new knowledge, methodologies and initiatives. We enable ethically minded entrepreneurs to build solutions that benefit people, society and the world. The Center experiments with new entrepreneurial methodologies and activities to push boundaries within research and education.

DTU – For the benefit of society since 1829
DTU is one of Europe's leading elite technical universities. Through research and education at an international top level, we create solutions to the major societal challenges of our time and help secure Europe's global leadership in sustainable technological development. Since Hans Christian Ørsted founded DTU almost 200 years ago, our mission has remained the same: We develop and create value through the natural and technical sciences for the benefit of society. DTU has 13,800 students, 1,600 PhD students, and 6,500 employees. We work in an international environment and have an inclusive, stimulating, and informal work culture. DTU has campuses in all parts of Denmark and in Greenland and collaborates with the best universities around the world.

jobs.occupation: Advanced Laboratory Technician - In Vivo Pharmacology
jobs.description:
Join a research environment where your work directly supports the discovery of future therapies for obesity, diabetes and cardiovascular disease. As an Advanced Laboratory Technician, you will plan, conduct and report preclinical large animal studies, generating high-quality data that helps move research programs forward. Working closely with scientists and fellow laboratory technicians, you will contribute to studies that are critical to our research pipeline and our ambition to drive scientific innovation.

The role is primarily based in Ganløse, however working cross functional means that some activities and meetings will take place in Måløv.

Your new role

As an Advanced Laboratory Technician, you will take end-to-end ownership of in vivo pharmacology studies preferably in large animals, working closely with scientists to deliver high-quality experimental outcomes that support our drug discovery projects

Your main responsibilities will be:

• Plan, conduct and report preclinical pharmacology studies, primarily in large animal models, supporting research within obesity, diabetes and cardiovascular disease.

• Perform a range of in vivo procedures, including dosing, blood sampling, tissue collection and surgical procedures, while ensuring high scientific and ethical standards.

• Generate high-quality data and documentation that support decision-making across research projects.

• Collaborate closely with scientists and fellow laboratory technicians to plan studies, share knowledge and achieve project goals.

• Maintain accurate study documentation and data records using electronic laboratory systems.

• Contribute to a safe, efficient and collaborative laboratory environment while supporting continuous improvements in ways of working.

Your new department

You will join a collaborative team of 10 laboratory technicians working closely together in our large animal research facility. Teamwork is an essential part of everyday work, from study planning to execution, and colleagues rely on one another to ensure high-quality research outcomes.

The team is part of Obesity and Comorbidities Pharmacology and supports research across obesity, diabetes and cardiovascular disease. Working alongside multidisciplinary project teams, you will contribute to studies that help generate the insights needed to advance future therapies.

Your skills and qualifications

We are looking for a laboratory technician who enjoys hands-on research and thrives in a collaborative environment. You bring experience from in vivo studies and are motivated by contributing to high-quality science that supports the discovery of future therapies.

To succeed in this role, you have:

• A Laboratory Technician degree or a similar qualification within biomedical sciences, pharmacology or a related field.

• Hands-on experience working with in vivo studies.

• Experience performing in vivo procedures and handling experimental data and study documentation.

• Familiarity with electronic laboratory documentation systems.

• Strong collaboration and communication skills, with the ability to work effectively across different disciplines.

• Experience working with large animal models is considered an advantage.

You work in a structured and quality-focused manner and take pride in delivering reliable results. You enjoy working closely with colleagues, sharing knowledge and supporting team success. As a person, you are pragmatic, approachable and eager to learn, with a strong sense of responsibility and respect for the ethical standards required in animal research. You are equally comfortable contributing to established ways of working and identifying opportunities to improve processes and laboratory practices.

Working at Novo

Every day we seek the solutions that defeat serious chronic diseases. To do this, we approach our work with determination, constant curiosity and a commitment to finding better ways forward. For over 100 years, this dedication has driven us to build a company focused on lasting change for long-term health. One where diverse thinking, shared purpose and mutual respect come together to create extraordinary results. Your impact begins here

Join us as a Senior Regulatory Affairs Professional and help turn scientific innovation into medicines that can reach patients worldwide. You will guide global regulatory submissions, shape interactions with Health Authorities and contribute to labelling strategies throughout the product lifecycle. Working with colleagues across research, development, safety, clinical operations and commercial functions, you will translate complex requirements into clear regulatory direction and deliver outcomes with global impact.

What you’ll bring

To succeed in this role, you have a strong scientific foundation and relevant experience in pharmaceutical development or Regulatory Affairs.

We expect you to have:

• A master’s degree in life sciences combined with approximately 5-7 years of relevant experience, or a PhD combined with approximately 3-4 years of relevant experience

• Alternatively, a bachelor’s degree in life sciences combined with approximately 8-11 years of relevant experience or equivalent knowledge gained through practical experience

• Experience with regulatory submissions and requirements in one or more major markets, such as the EU, US, China or Japan

• Knowledge of early- or late-stage drug development, lifecycle management, labelling or Health Authority interactions

• Strong written and spoken English

• The ability to interpret complex scientific and regulatory information and communicate it clearly to different audiences

• Confidence working independently, setting priorities and managing several complex deliverables

Experience within areas such as clinical development, pharmacovigilance, medical devices, regulatory intelligence, market access or project management would be useful.

You work with a strategic mindset and can make sound decisions based on risk evaluation. You are structured, accountable and comfortable adjusting your approach in a changing environment. You also build trusting relationships, contribute actively across teams and communicate with professional authority while remaining open to different perspectives.

What you’ll do

Your primary responsibility will be to develop and execute regulatory activities that support global drug development and lifecycle management.

Your key responsibilities will include:

• Planning and coordinating global regulatory submissions, including marketing authorisation applications, clinical trial applications and lifecycle-management submissions.

• Applying regulatory intelligence to develop submission strategies, plans, content structures and timelines

• Preparing regulatory files and coordinating document creation, review, and submission

• Managing responses, commitments and follow-up activities arising from Health Authority

• Planning and supporting interactions with Health Authorities, including meeting requests, briefing packages, rehearsals and formal meeting documentation

• Developing and maintaining core labelling, including the Company Core Data Sheet and European labelling

• Contributing to global regulatory strategies and identifying opportunities to improve methods, processes and regulatory approaches

• Providing regulatory guidance to stakeholders and mentoring less-experienced colleagues when relevant

You will independently manage most situations and take initiative when planning and delivering your work. More complex matters will be addressed in close collaboration with specialists, senior colleagues and your manager.

Who you’ll work with

You will join Regulatory Affairs within Obesity & Cardiometabolic Health and work in a global, cross-functional environment. Your closest collaboration partners may include colleagues from, Clinical reporting, Medical and Translational Science, Clinical Operations, Global Safety, Medical Affairs, Commercial,, Legal, Quality and Regulatory Affairs teams across headquarters and affiliates.

Externally, you may engage with Health Authorities such as the European Medicines Agency, the US Food and Drug Administration, Japan’s Pharmaceuticals and Medical Devices Agency and other regulatory agencies worldwide.

The role requires you to create alignment across different professional disciplines, organisational areas and regions. You will often communicate complex or ambiguous information, navigate different interests and help stakeholders reach decisions that support both regulatory requirements and business priorities.

Do you thrive in a fast-paced, global environment where you can influence leaders, drive organisational development and deliver impactful people initiatives to create lasting health for our customers? Then you may be the Associated P&O Business Partner we are looking for in Drug Product Manufacturing, Expansions (DPM Expansions).

Your new role

As Associated P&O Business Partner, you will shape the people agenda that helps DPM Expansions build Novo’s future manufacturing capacity. Working with senior leaders and expansion sites globally, you will turn business priorities into practical people and organisational plans – from workforce planning and capability building to leadership, culture and change. Your work will help teams grow with confidence and speed, so new capacity can reach the people who rely on our treatments faster.

Your day-to-day tasks will include:

• Partner with leaders at our QC expansion in Hillerød to translate business priorities into people and organisational strategies.

• Advise and challenge leaders on organisational development, strategic workforce planning, capability building, culture, leadership and engagement.

• Support leadership teams through organisational change and transformation as the expansion site scale up.

• Facilitate talent, performance, succession and development discussions, and support annual people processes.

• Use people insights and analytics so leaders can make data-driven decisions.

• Lead strategic P&O activities and projects across our global expansions - from plan to delivery, including work that supports a fleet manufacturing mindset, employee engagement and onboarding - and  shared ways of working across sites that help us deliver to customers faster.

Your new department

You will join DPM Expansions, which builds future-proof manufacturing capacity for Novo. You will report to Associate Director Pernille Albrechtsen, DPM Expansions P&O..

You will join our People & Organisation Business Partnering team consisting of several P&O Business Partners in Denmark and on global sites where we are executing manufacturing expansions. You will also work with P&O Centres of Excellence and leaders from expansion sites around the world.

It is a highly collaborative, international setting.

Your skills & qualifications

You combine strategic thinking with hands-on delivery, and you enjoy working across organisational boundaries. You will bring:

• A degree within HR, Psychology, or Business Management (or you might be from a completely different field or a former experienced Manager moving into HR—what matters most is excellent people and leadership skills)

• A self-motivated, solution-driven attitude with high energy and the ability to create trust while motivating collaboration across all levels of an organization

• The ability to set direction and make things happen, while knowing when to look for alternatives in an ever-changing environment with sharp deadlines

• Strong analytical skills with a structured approach to solving challenges and finding insights in data

• Excellent listening skills and a proactive mindset—you're a great colleague who seeks to contribute

• Project management experience and experience from working in a global environment is an advantage

• Fluency in English.
